source_text: De fide contra Arianos (fragmenta) 63 Ἀρχὴ γάρ τοι τῶν καλλίστων τῆς δικαιοσύνης ὁδῶν γεγένηται ἡμῖν ὁ ἄνθρωπος τοῦ Χριστοῦ, τοῖς κρείττοσι τῶν ἐπιτηδευμάτων προσάγων ἡμᾶς. Σεμνοπρεπῶς προσαρμόττει τῷ Πνεύματι, ξεναγεῖ εἰς τὸν παράδεισον, εἰς τὴν οἰκείαν ἀποκαθίστησι νομήν. ∆ιὸ καὶ ὁ Χριστὸς ἔλεγεν· ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ ὁδὸς καὶ ἡ ἀλήθεια καὶ ἡ ζωή. Τῷ μὲν οὖν ὀνόματι τῆς ὁδοῦ τὴν κατὰ ἄνθρωπον δηλοῖ περιβολὴν, ὅπερ ἔστι τῶν σωματικῶν καὶ τῶν ὁρατῶν· γῆς γάρ τι μόριον ἡ ὁδὸς καὶ αἰσθητὸν ἔδαφος καθέστηκε· τὸ δὲ ὄνομα τῆς ἀληθείας <καὶ> τῆς ζωῆς τὴν τοῦ Πατρὸς φύσιν· ἡ γὰρ ἀλήθεια πρᾶγμά τι νοητὸν οὔτε ὄμμασιν οὔτε ἁφῇ ὑποπίπτον.
thought_title: The manhood of Christ as the way to the Father's truth and life
orientation: Eustathius opens his treatise by presenting the manhood of Christ as the starting point of the fairest paths of righteousness, then interprets Christ's saying 'I am the way and the truth and the life.'
pass_a_gloss: For indeed the manhood of Christ has become for us the beginning of the fairest ways of righteousness, leading us to the better pursuits. Fittingly it joins us to the Spirit, it guides us into paradise, it restores us to the proper pasture. Therefore Christ also said: I am the way and the truth and the life. By the name of the way, then, he indicates the covering according to man, which is of the bodily and of the visible things; for the way is a portion of earth and has been established as a perceptible ground; but the name of the truth and of the life indicates the nature of the Father; for truth is an intelligible thing falling under neither eyes nor touch.

pass_b_english: For the manhood of Christ has become for us the starting point of the fairest ways of righteousness, leading us to better pursuits. It fittingly joins us to the Spirit, guides us into paradise, and restores us to our proper pasture. Therefore Christ said, “I am the way and the truth and the life” (John 14:6). By the name “way” he indicates the covering according to the manhood, which belongs to bodily and visible things; for a way is a portion of earth and a perceptible ground. But the name “truth” and “life” indicates the nature of the Father; for truth is an intelligible thing that falls under neither sight nor touch.

last_rejected.why: Subject is 'the manhood of Christ' (neuter 'It'), but Greek 'Σεμνοπρεπῶς προσαρμόττει' has no expressed subject; 'It' refers back correctly. No error.
last_rejected.ruling: No expressed subject in Greek; 'It' correctly refers to preceding 'manhood of Christ.' No error.

last_rejected.why: English correctly marks Christ as speaker per voices brief. No error.
last_rejected.ruling: ὁ Χριστὸς ἔλεγεν correctly rendered 'Christ said'; speaker identification is accurate.

last_rejected.why: The scripture brief says 'The fragment quotes John 14:6' and the English correctly cites it. No error.
last_rejected.ruling: Quote matches John 14:6 exactly; scripture reference is correct.

last_rejected.quote: which belongs to bodily and visible things
last_rejected.source_quote: ὅπερ ἔστι τῶν σωματικῶν καὶ τῶν ὁρατῶν
last_rejected.why: 'belongs to' weakens the force; Greek 'ὅπερ ἔστι' = 'which is among/belongs to' but more naturally 'which is of bodily and visible things.' However, 'belongs to' is within semantic range. No error.
last_rejected.ruling: 'belongs to' is within normal semantic range of ὅπερ ἔστι τῶν σωματικῶν; mere preference.

last_rejected.quote: and restores us to our proper pasture
last_rejected.why: Checking: 'restores us to our proper pasture' — 'οἰκείαν' = 'proper/own', 'νομήν' = 'pasture'. English adds 'us' but Greek has it as object of previous verbs; 'ἀποκαθίστησι' takes the same 'us' implied. No error.
last_rejected.ruling: 'us' implied from previous verbs ἡμᾶς; ἀποκαθίστησι carries same object. No addition.
